I am ready to play Monopoly and make a decision.

I am player p2 with $3711 and three hotels. The opponent has only $29 and is almost fully mortgaged, leaving dark blues as their main threat. I have two get-out-of-jail cards.

I will keep both get-out-of-jail cards and avoid selling hotels or unmortgaging the railroads. The opponent's dark blue properties are too expensive to threaten with my current cash.

I can afford both dark blue hotels. I am checking the board order to see if the opponent can land on my pink hotels.

The opponent on Kentucky Avenue is too far from my pink hotels to land there. They would need to go almost the full loop and collect $200 before reaching them.

I counted the exact board positions from Atlantic Avenue. Only a roll of 11 would land on Park Place, which I can easily afford. I am now deciding whether to take any optional actions this turn or simply end it.

I considered proposing a trade. Giving the opponent Tennessee would complete their orange set and help them build more. They would not likely trade away their dark blue hotels for anything I have.

I will not offer cash or trade this turn. Unmortgaging the railroads would cost more than their rent and give no set benefit, so that is also a bad idea.

I calculated the opponent's maximum liquidation. They could sell seven dark blue houses for $700, mortgage Vermont for $50, and collect $200 from passing GO. Their total would reach about $979.
